config.title: Build type safe form schema builder

intro.title: Build type safe form schema builder
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a type-safe form schema builder using TypeScript. You will create a function that defines form fields with specific data types and validation rules. The core concept is leveraging TypeScript's generic types and interfaces to ensure your form data is checked at compile time. You will work with key TypeScript constructs like generics, type parameters, and return type inference. By the end, you'll have a reusable, type-safe utility that prevents common form errors before your code even runs.
intro.usecase: Type-safe form schemas are essential in enterprise applications like customer relationship management (CRM) systems, where complex data entry forms with validation rules must be reliably processed. Developers use this pattern when building admin dashboards for e-commerce platforms to ensure product listings, pricing configurations, and inventory updates maintain data integrity. In financial software, loan application forms and investment portals leverage type-safe schemas to prevent submission errors and enforce business logic constraints. This approach also powers dynamic form builders in content management systems (CMS) where editors can safely create custom data collection interfaces without breaking the underlying data model.

objectives: Construct a TypeScript interface to define the structure of a form schema.
Implement a function that validates form data against the defined schema.
Apply generic types to create a reusable schema builder function.
Configure type-safe error handling for invalid form inputs.
Integrate the schema builder with a sample form component.
Manipulate form state using the schema to ensure data integrity.
Render form validation feedback based on the schema rules.

steps.title: Import TypeScript types and utilities
steps.instruction: Import the necessary TypeScript types and utilities for building type-safe form schemas. Import the following: `z` from 'zod', `FieldValues` and `UseFormReturn` from 'react-hook-form', and `FormField` from '@/components/ui/form'.
steps.hint: Use import statements to bring in the required dependencies. Remember to use the correct import paths.

steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary imports for building type-safe form schemas are added to the file.
successCriteria: The file contains imports for `z` from 'zod', `FieldValues` and `UseFormReturn` from 'react-hook-form', and `FormField` from '@/components/ui/form'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some of the required utilities, but not all. Make sure to import `z` from 'zod', `FieldValues` and `UseFormReturn` from 'react-hook-form', and `FormField` from '@/components/ui/form'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import `z` from 'zod', `FieldValues` and `UseFormReturn` from 'react-hook-form', and `FormField` from '@/components/ui/form' to proceed.

steps.title: Define the base FormField interface
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface called FormField with name, label, and required properties.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions with appropriate types.
steps.seedCode:
// Import the required types and utilities here

// Define the FormField interface below
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a FormField interface with name (string), label (string), and required (boolean) properties.
successCriteria: The FormField interface is defined with name: string, label: string, and required: boolean properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the interface is missing some required properties. Make sure to include name, label, and required with their correct TypeScript types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The FormField interface isn't defined correctly. Remember to use the 'interface' keyword and include all three properties with appropriate types.

steps.title: Create specific field type interfaces
steps.instruction: Create three specialized interfaces that extend the FormField interface: TextField, NumberField, and SelectField.
steps.hint: Use the 'extends' keyword to create interfaces that inherit from FormField, then add type-specific properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have three new interfaces that extend FormField with type-specific properties for different form field types.
successCriteria: The code contains TextField, NumberField, and SelectField interfaces that extend FormField with appropriate additional properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created some of the required interfaces, but need all three: TextField, NumberField, and SelectField.
steps.feedbackWrong: The specialized interfaces are missing or don't properly extend FormField. Make sure to use the 'extends' keyword and add appropriate properties for each field type.

steps.title: Define the FormSchema type
steps.instruction: Define a type named FormSchema that represents an array of FormField objects.
steps.hint: Use the type keyword with an array type annotation using FormField[].
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: a type for a collection of items
type ItemList = Item[];
steps.expectedOutcome: A FormSchema type is defined as an array of FormField objects.
successCriteria: FormSchema type is defined with type FormSchema = FormField[].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a type-safe collection of form fields.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure FormSchema is defined as an array of FormField objects.
steps.feedbackWrong: The FormSchema type should be defined as an array of FormField objects.

steps.title: Create the form schema builder function
steps.instruction: Create a function named createFormSchema that accepts an array of FormField objects and returns a FormSchema.
steps.hint: Define a function with a parameter typed as FormField[] and a return type of FormSchema.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a function that can build type-safe form schemas from field definitions.
successCriteria: The createFormSchema function is defined with proper TypeScript types for its parameter and return value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your function accepts FormField[] and returns FormSchema with explicit types.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the function signature. It should accept an array of FormField objects and return a FormSchema.

steps.title: Add validation rules to field interfaces
steps.instruction: Add optional validation properties to the TextField and NumberField interfaces. For TextField, add minLength?: number, maxLength?: number, and pattern?: string. For NumberField, add min?: number and max?: number.
steps.hint: Extend the existing interfaces by adding optional properties with the ? modifier after the property name.
steps.expectedOutcome: The TextField and NumberField interfaces will include optional validation properties that can be used to enforce constraints on form input.
successCriteria: TextField interface has minLength?: number, maxLength?: number, and pattern?: string properties. NumberField interface has min?: number and max?: number properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added some validation properties, but not all required ones. Make sure TextField has minLength, maxLength, and pattern, and NumberField has min and max.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation properties weren't added correctly. Remember to add optional properties with ? to both TextField and NumberField interfaces.

steps.title: Create validation result types
steps.instruction: Create a ValidationResult interface to represent the outcome of validating a single field, and a FormValidationResult type for the overall form validation results.
steps.hint: Define ValidationResult with properties like isValid (boolean) and errorMessage (string). Then create FormValidationResult as a record mapping field names to ValidationResult objects.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have defined ValidationResult and FormValidationResult types to represent validation outcomes in your form schema builder.
successCriteria: ValidationResult interface and FormValidationResult type are defined with appropriate properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress, but make sure both ValidationResult (interface) and FormValidationResult (type) are defined with the correct structure.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation result types aren't defined correctly. Check that ValidationResult has isValid and optional errorMessage, and FormValidationResult maps field names to ValidationResult objects.

steps.title: Implement the validation function
steps.instruction: Create a function named validateForm that takes a FormSchema and form data object, and returns validation results.
steps.hint: Define a function with two parameters: schema (type FormSchema) and data (type Record<string, any>). Return an array of validation results.
steps.expectedOutcome: A validateForm function is added to the codebase with proper TypeScript parameters and return type.
successCriteria: The validateForm function is defined with two parameters (schema and data) and returns an array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function has both parameters (schema and data) and returns an array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validateForm function is missing or has incorrect structure. It should accept FormSchema and form data, then return validation results.

steps.title: Create a sample form schema
steps.instruction: Use the createFormSchema function to build a sample user registration form schema with at least three fields (e.g., name, email, age).
steps.hint: Call createFormSchema with an array of field objects that match the TextField and NumberField interfaces you defined earlier.
steps.expectedOutcome: A sample user registration form schema is created using the createFormSchema function.
successCriteria: The createFormSchema function is called with an array containing at least three field objects that match the TextField and NumberField interfaces.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the sample schema, but ensure you're calling createFormSchema with at least three field objects that match the defined interfaces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The sample schema wasn't created correctly. Remember to call createFormSchema with an array of field objects that match the TextField and NumberField interfaces.

steps.title: Test the validation with sample data
steps.instruction: Create a sample data object that matches the form structure and test it against your validateForm function.
steps.hint: Define an object with properties matching the field names from your sample form schema, then call validateForm with both the schema and data.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll see how the type-safe validation system catches errors in form data and returns structured validation results.
successCriteria: A sample data object is created and passed to validateForm along with the form schema, demonstrating type-safe validation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're calling validateForm with both the form schema and sample data object, and that your data matches the field names from your schema.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation test isn't working yet. Remember to create a sample data object with properties matching your form field names, then pass both the schema and data to validateForm.
